chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who does not fast the three days from every month, and fasting is difficult upon him. Is there a redemption (expiation) for it? He (peace be upon him) said: A Mudd of food for each day.

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A Mudd (a specific volume measure of food, approx. 750g)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for missing the three days of fasting each month?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the specific expiation (*fidyah*) for neglecting the *Ayyam al-Beed* (the 13th, 14th, and 15th days of the lunar month), prescribing a *Mudd* of food per missed day. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the distinction between the voluntary nature of these fasts and the mandatory compensation required for their omission, reflecting the practical flexibility (*rukhas*) granted to believers. The *Mudd* typically corresponds to approximately 750 grams of wheat or rice, serving as a tangible act of charity to compensate for the missed spiritual merit.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one who does not Fast the three days from every month, and the Fasting is difficult upon him. Is there a redemption in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of food regarding each day’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who does not fast three days every month because fasting is difficult for him: if there is a ransom for it. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is one mud (a certain measurement) of food for everyday.’”
